page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The diagonal pairs
lines: In the second and third periods an
diagonally below it and to the right.
This likeness is called the diagonal
The pairs are Li and Mg, Be and Al,
steps.why: The question asks for reasons, so the answer must first say which pairs it is about: a diagonal relationship is a property of two elements taken together, not of one element on its own.
common_mistakes: Naming two elements of the same group. A diagonal pair lies in different groups and different periods.
Writing only the word similarity. Name at least one pair, such as Li and Mg.
steps.memory_tip: Move one step to the right and one step down: Li to Mg, Be to Al, B to Si.
steps.margin_note: Name one diagonal pair before giving the reasons.

steps.label: The reasons
lines: Across a period the atomic and ionic
Down a group the size rises and
Along a diagonal the two changes cancel.
So a diagonal pair has a similar ionic
size, a similar charge to size ratio
steps.why: The diagonal relationship is not a separate rule. It follows from two periodic trends acting in opposite directions, which leave a diagonal pair close in ionic size, in charge to size ratio and in electronegativity. How close each of the three is varies from one pair to the next — for Be and Al the charge to size ratios are very nearly equal — so the three are written as the reasons for the likeness, not as three exact equalities.
common_mistakes: Naming the trend without saying what it leaves similar — the size and the electronegativity of the pair.
Writing that size increases across a period. Size decreases across a period and increases down a group.
steps.memory_tip: A step to the right lowers the size, a step down raises it, so the diagonal step leaves size, charge to size ratio and electronegativity nearly unchanged.
steps.margin_note: State both trends; the cancelling is what makes the pair alike.

insider_note: The reasons are the two opposite periodic trends and the three properties they leave nearly equal: ionic size, charge to size ratio and electronegativity.
